[RTIM.14.14] **A step the engine refuses fails the case.** The interpreter
drives a case by operations that each return a status: a cache seed, an
arrange or input assertion, a reply's assertion, a clock move and a pump
([RTIM.14.4], [RTIM.14.5], [RTIM.14.6]). When one returns anything but success,
whether or not the engine halted ([NCBK.2.9]), the interpreter **must** fail
the case, naming the operation and its status, and **must** stop driving the
case there: it delivers no later instant and no later reply. It **may** report
the case's assertions over what it observed until then. The case does not pass
on them.

No assertion head observes a refused step ([LTSL.8.2]): a pump that refuses a
cache write past its cap or drops a call on a NaN argument leaves nothing an
assertion could read. So a refusal the interpreter passed over would let a
program that breaks a bound pass a test that never looked for it.
